questions.question: A chat service has high time to first token but stable time per output token. Which path should be investigated first?
options: Admission queue, prefix reuse, and prefill
The number of completed output tokens
questions.explanation: TTFT ends at the first streamed token, so queueing, routing, cache lookup, and prefill are the direct stages to break down first.

questions.question: What does automatic prefix caching directly avoid when an exact reusable prefix matches?
questions.explanation: Prefix caching reuses KV state created for matching input tokens. It reduces prefill work, but new output tokens still require decode.

questions.question: A model has 40 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, and a 2-byte KV data type. Approximately how many KV bytes does one token require before runtime overhead?
questions.explanation: Keys and values require 2 x 40 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 163,840 bytes per token before layout and allocator overhead.

questions.question: Why can a larger batching window be harmful to an interactive product even when throughput improves?
options: Waiting for the batch consumes the TTFT budget
It changes the model's training labels
It always disables the KV cache
It forces every token to use higher precision
questions.explanation: Batch formation adds queueing before prefill. Throughput must therefore be compared at the required TTFT and TPOT SLO.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates exact speculative decoding from quantization?
options: Exact speculative sampling can preserve the target distribution, while quantization still needs task-quality evaluation
Both techniques are guaranteed to preserve every output bit-for-bit
Quantization preserves the distribution, while speculation always changes it
Neither technique changes capacity or memory requirements
questions.explanation: Exact speculative algorithms verify draft tokens against the target distribution. Quantization changes numerical representation and can alter outputs.

questions.question: A 70-billion-parameter model uses 4 bits per weight. What is its approximate raw weight storage before scales, metadata, padding, and runtime state?
questions.explanation: 70 billion x 4 bits / 8 bits per byte is approximately 35 GB of raw weight data. Serving needs additional memory.

questions.question: What is the strongest capacity metric for a user-facing serving pool?
options: Useful requests or tokens completed inside the latency and quality contract
Maximum tokens generated after all deadlines are removed
Average GPU utilization without workload slices
questions.explanation: Goodput ties capacity to the product contract. Raw throughput can include late, cancelled, or low-quality work.
